readings.title: The Preparation of the Ashes
readings.subtitle: Establishing the physical elements to transition the people from Tame (unfit) to Tahor (fit for purpose).
readings.text:
[Numbers 19:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying,
[2] <dq>This is a law of the Torah which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded, saying, ‘Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, that they bring you <dn>את</dn> a red heifer, a perfect one, in which there is no blemish and on which a yoke has never come.</dq>
[3] <dq>And you shall give <dn>את</dn> it to El‛azar the priest, and he shall bring it outside the camp, and shall slay it before him.</dq>
[4] <dq>And El‛azar the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger, and sprinkle some of its blood seven times toward the front of the Tent of Appointment.</dq>
[5] <dq>And the heifer shall be burned before his eyes – he burns <dn>את</dn> its hide, and <dn>את</dn> its flesh, and <dn>את</dn> its blood, and <dn>את</dn> its dung.</dq>
[6] <dq>And the priest shall take <dn>את</dn> cedar wood and hyssop and scarlet, and throw them into the midst of the fire burning the heifer.</dq>
[7] <dq>The priest shall then wash his garments, and shall bathe his body in water, and afterward come into the camp, but the priest is unclean until evening.</dq>
[8] <dq>And he who is burning it washes his garments in water, and shall bathe his body in water, and is unclean until evening.</dq>
[9] <dq>And a clean man shall gather up <dn>את</dn> the ashes of the heifer, and shall place them outside the camp in a clean place. And they shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Yisra’ěl for the water for uncleanness, it is for cleansing from sin.</dq>
[10] <dq>And he who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his garments, and is unclean until evening. And it shall be a law forever to the children of Yisra’ěl and to the stranger who sojourns in their midst.</dq>

readings.title: Restoring the Unfit
readings.subtitle: Strict protocols for restoring those rendered structurally unfit by the ultimate enemy, death.
readings.text:
[Numbers 19:11] <dq>He who touches the dead of any human being is unclean for seven days.</dq>
[12] <dq>He is to cleanse himself with the water on the third day, and on the seventh day he is clean. But if he does not cleanse himself on the third day, then on the seventh day he is not clean.</dq>
[13] <dq>Anyone who touches the dead of a human being, and does not cleanse himself, defiles <dn>את</dn> the Dwelling Place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And that being shall be cut off from Yisra’ěl. He is unclean, for the water for uncleanness was not sprinkled on him, his uncleanness is still upon him.</dq>
[14] <dq>This is <dn>את</dn> the Torah when a man dies in a tent: All who come into the tent and all who are in the tent are unclean for seven days,</dq>
[15] <dq>and every open vessel which has no cover fastened on it, is unclean.</dq>
[16] <dq>Anyone in the open field who touches someone slain by a sword or who has died, or a bone of a man, or a burial-site, is unclean for seven days.</dq>
[17] <dq>And for the unclean being they shall take some of the ashes of the heifer burnt for cleansing from sin, and running water shall be put on them in a vessel.</dq>
[18] <dq>And a clean man shall take hyssop and dip it in the water, and shall sprinkle <dn>את</dn> it on the tent, and on <dn>את</dn> all the vessels, and on <dn>את</dn> the beings who were there, or on <dn>את</dn> the one who touched a bone, or <dn>את</dn> the slain, or <dn>את</dn> the dead, or <dn>את</dn> a burial-site.</dq>
[19] <dq>And the clean one shall sprinkle the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day. And on the seventh day he shall cleanse himself, and shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and shall be clean in the evening.</dq>
[20] <dq>But the man who is unclean and does not cleanse himself, that being shall be cut off from among the assembly, because he has defiled <dn>את</dn> the set-apart place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – water for uncleanness has not been sprinkled on him, he is unclean.</dq>
[21] <dq>And it shall be a law for them forever. And the one who sprinkles the water for uncleanness washes his garments. And the one who touches the water for uncleanness is unclean until evening.</dq>
[22] <dq>And whatever the unclean being touches is unclean. And the being who touches it is unclean until evening.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Death of Miryam and the Thirst of the Assembly
readings.subtitle: The congregation suffers physical lack and complains against YeHoVaH's appointed leaders.
readings.text:
[Numbers 20:1] And the children of Yisra’ěl, all the congregation, came into the Wilderness of Tsin in the first new moon, and the people stayed in Qaḏěsh. And Miryam died there and was buried there.
[2] Now there was no water for the congregation and they assembled against Mosheh and against Aharon.
[3] And the people contended with Mosheh and spoke, saying, “If only we had died when our brothers died before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!
[4] “Why have you brought up the assembly of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> into this wilderness, that we and our livestock should die here?
[5] “And why have you brought us up out of Mitsrayim, to bring us to this evil place? – not a place of grain or figs or vines or pomegranates, and there is no water to drink.”

readings.title: Mosheh Strikes the Rock
readings.subtitle: A failure to exactly execute the word and trust of YeHoVaH strips Mosheh of entry into the land.
readings.text:
[Numbers 20:6] Then Mosheh and Aharon went from the presence of the assembly to the door of the Tent of Appointment, and they fell on their faces. And the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to them.
[7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying,
[8] <dq>Take <dn>את</dn> the rod and assemble <dn>את</dn> the congregation, you and your brother Aharon. And you shall speak to the rock before their eyes, and it shall give its water. And you shall bring water for them out of the rock and give drink to the congregation and their livestock.</dq>
[9] And Mosheh took <dn>את</dn> the rod from before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> as <dn>He</dn> commanded him.
[10] And Mosheh and Aharon assembled <dn>את</dn> the assembly before the rock. And he said to them, “Hear now, you rebels, shall we bring water for you out of this rock?”
[11] Then Mosheh lifted his hand and struck <dn>את</dn> the rock twice with his rod. And much water came out, and the congregation and their livestock drank.
[12] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, <dq>Because you did not believe <dn>Me</dn>, to set <dn>Me</dn> apart in the eyes of the children of Yisra’ěl, therefore you do not bring this assembly into the land which <dn>I</dn> have given them.</dq>
[13] These were the waters of Meriḇah, because the children of Yisra’ěl contended with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> was set apart among them.

readings.section: The Journey to the Promised Land
readings.title: Eḏom Refuses Passage to Yisra’ěl
readings.subtitle: The descendants of Ěsaw deny their brothers the right to traverse the sovereign's highway.
readings.text:
[Numbers 20:14] And Mosheh sent messengers from Qaḏěsh to the sovereign of Eḏom. “This is what your brother Yisra’ěl said, ‘You know <dn>את</dn> all the hardship that has befallen us,
[15] that our fathers went down to Mitsrayim, and we dwelt in Mitsrayim a long time, and the Mitsrites did evil to us and our fathers.
[16] And we cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> heard our voice and sent <dn>את</dn> the Messenger and brought us up out of Mitsrayim. And see, we are in Qaḏěsh, a city on the edge of your border.
[17] Please let us pass over, through your land. We shall not pass over through fields or vineyards, nor drink water from wells, we shall go along the sovereign’s highway. We shall not turn aside, right or left, until we have passed over your border.’ ”
[18] But Eḏom said to him, “You do not pass over through me, lest I come out against you with the sword.”
[19] And the children of Yisra’ěl said to him, “We shall go by the highway, and if I or my livestock drink any of your water, then I shall pay for it. Let me only pass over on foot, without a word.”
[20] But he said, “You do not pass over.” And Eḏom came out against them with many men and with a strong hand.
[21] So when Eḏom refused to let Yisra’ěl pass over through his border, Yisra’ěl turned away from him.

readings.section: The Journey to the Promised Land
readings.title: The Death of Aharon
readings.subtitle: The high priesthood transfers to El‛azar as Aharon is gathered to his people.
readings.text:
[Numbers 20:22] And the children of Yisra’ěl, all the company, departed from Qaḏěsh and came to Mount Hor.
[23] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon in Mount Hor near the border of the land of Eḏom, saying,
[24] <dq>Aharon is to be gathered to his people, for he is not to enter the land which <dn>I</dn> have given to the children of Yisra’ěl, because you rebelled against <dn>My</dn> mouth at the water of Meriḇah.</dq>
[25] <dq>Take <dn>את</dn> Aharon and <dn>את</dn> El‛azar his son, and bring them up to Mount Hor,</dq>
[26] <dq>and strip <dn>את</dn> Aharon of his garments and put <dn>את</dn> them on El‛azar his son, for Aharon is to be gathered to his people and die there.</dq>
[27] And Mosheh did as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded, and they went up to Mount Hor before the eyes of all the congregation.
[28] And Mosheh stripped <dn>את</dn> Aharon of his garments and put <dn>את</dn> them on El‛azar his son. And Aharon died there on the top of the mountain. And Mosheh and El‛azar came down from the mountain.
[29] And when all the congregation saw that Aharon was dead, all the house of Yisra’ěl wept for Aharon, thirty days.

readings.title: Victory Over the Kena‛anites of Araḏ
readings.subtitle: Yisra’ěl relies entirely on YeHoVaH to put their enemies under the ban.
readings.text:
[Numbers 21:1] And the sovereign of Araḏ, the Kena‛anite, who dwelt in the South, heard that Yisra’ěl was coming on the way to Atharim, and he fought against Yisra’ěl and took some of them captive.
[2] Then Yisra’ěl made a vow to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “If You deliver <dn>את</dn> this people into my hand indeed, then I shall put their cities under the ban.”
[3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> listened to the voice of Yisra’ěl and gave up <dn>את</dn> the Kena‛anites, and they put <dn>את</dn> them and <dn>את</dn> their cities under the ban. So the name of that place was called Ḥormah.

readings.title: The Bronze Serpent
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH deploys a bronze serpent for Tov (harmony), providing a strict physical focal point for deliverance from death.
readings.text:
[Numbers 21:4] And they departed from Mount Hor by the Way of the Sea of Reeds, to go around the land of Eḏom. But the being of the people grew impatient because of the way.
[5] And the people spoke against <dn>Elohim</dn> and against Mosheh, “Why have you brought us up out of Mitsrayim to die in the wilderness? For there is no food and no water, and our being loathes this light bread.”
[6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent <dn>את</dn> fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people. And many of the people of Yisra’ěl died.
[7] Then the people came to Mosheh, and said, “We have sinned, for we have spoken against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and against you. Pray to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to take away <dn>את</dn> the serpents from us.” So Mosheh prayed on behalf of the people.
[8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>Make a fiery serpent, and set it on a pole. And it shall be that everyone who is bitten, when he looks at it, shall live.</dq>
[9] So Mosheh made a bronze serpent, and put <dn>את</dn> it on a pole. And it came to be, if a serpent had bitten anyone, when he looked at the bronze serpent, he lived.

readings.section: The Journey to the Promised Land
readings.title: Setting Out to the Arnon
readings.subtitle: Yisra’ěl traverses the geographic boundaries dividing the Amorites and Mo’aḇ.
readings.text:
[Numbers 21:10] And the children of Yisra’ěl set out and camped in Oḇoth.
[11] And they departed from Oḇoth and camped at Iyě Ha-Aḇarim, in the wilderness which is east of Mo’aḇ, toward sunrise.
[12] From there they set out and camped at the wadi Zereḏ.
[13] From there they set out and camped on the other side of the Arnon, which is in the wilderness that extends from the border of the Amorites, for the Arnon is the border of Mo’aḇ, between Mo’aḇ and the Amorites.
[14] Therefore it is said in the Book of the Battles of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “<dn>את</dn> Wahěḇ in Suphah, <dn>את</dn> the wadi Arnon,
[15] and <dn>את</dn> the slope of the wadi that turns aside to the dwelling of Ar, and lies on the border of Mo’aḇ.”

readings.section: The Journey to the Promised Land
readings.title: The Song of the Well
readings.subtitle: The leaders of the assembly draw water by the word of the Inscriber.
readings.text:
[Numbers 21:16] And from there on to Be’ěr, which is the well where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>Gather the people, and let <dn>Me</dn> give them water.</dq>
[17] Yisra’ěl then sang this song: “Spring up, O well! Sing to it,
[18] a well the leaders sank, which the nobles of the people dug with their staves, by the word of the Inscriber.” Then from the wilderness on to Mattanah,
[19] from Mattanah to Naḥali’ěl, from Naḥali’ěl to Bamoth,
[20] and from Bamoth, in the valley that is in the country of Mo’aḇ, to the top of Pisgah which looks down on the wasteland.

readings.title: The Conquest of Siḥon
readings.subtitle: The systematic dismantling of the Amorite stronghold and the expansion of Yisra’ěl’s terrestrial authority.
readings.text:
[Numbers 21:21] And Yisra’ěl sent messengers to Siḥon sovereign of the Amorites, saying,
[22] “Let me pass through your land. We shall not turn off into fields or vineyards, we shall not drink water from wells, but go by the sovereign’s highway until we have passed over your border.”
[23] But Siḥon would not allow Yisra’ěl to pass through his border. So Siḥon gathered <dn>את</dn> all his people together and went out against Yisra’ěl in the wilderness, and he came to Yahats and fought against Yisra’ěl.
[24] And Yisra’ěl struck <dn>את</dn> him with the edge of the sword, and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Yabboq, as far as the children of Ammon, for the border of the children of Ammon was strong.
[25] And Yisra’ěl took <dn>את</dn> all these cities, and Yisra’ěl dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites – in Ḥeshbon and in all its villages,
[26] for Ḥeshbon was the city of Siḥon the sovereign of the Amorites, who had fought against the former sovereign of Mo’aḇ, and had taken <dn>את</dn> all his land from his hand as far as the Arnon.
[27] That is why those who speak in proverbs say, “Come to Ḥeshbon, let the city of Siḥon be built and established.
[28] “For fire went out from Ḥeshbon, a flame from the city of Siḥon. It consumed <dn>את</dn> Ar of Mo’aḇ, <dn>את</dn> the masters of the heights of the Arnon.
[29] “Woe to you, Mo’aḇ! You have perished, O people of Kemosh! He has given <dn>את</dn> his sons as fugitives, and <dn>את</dn> his daughters into captivity, to Siḥon the sovereign of the Amorites.
[30] “Then we shot them – Ḥeshbon has perished as far as Diḇon. And we laid waste as far as Nophaḥ, which reaches to Měyḏeḇa.”

readings.title: The Defeat of Oḡ
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH delivers the giant king and his people entirely into the hand of Yisra’ěl.
readings.text:
[Numbers 21:31] So Yisra’ěl dwelt in the land of the Amorites.
[32] And Mosheh sent to spy out <dn>את</dn> Ya‛zěr. And they took its villages and drove out <dn>את</dn> the Amorites who were there,
[33] and turned and went up by the way to Bashan. And Oḡ sovereign of Bashan went out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Eḏre‛i.
[34] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>Do not fear him, for <dn>I</dn> have given him into your hand, with all his people and his land. And you shall do to him as you did to Siḥon sovereign of the Amorites, who dwelt at Ḥeshbon.</dq>
[35] And they struck <dn>את</dn> him, and <dn>את</dn> his sons, and <dn>את</dn> all his people, until no remnant was left to him. And they took possession of his land.
